observation.visible_scene: A close-up, static nighttime shot of a small open fire burning on a pile of folded, yellowish paper-like pieces resting on a gray ashy base with a band of reddish glowing embers across the middle. A dark vertical pillar/wall frames the left edge and a green cartoon logo sits in the top-left corner; faint brick-like structure on the right is intermittently lit by the flames. The background is otherwise black.
visible_changes: Flames flicker and continuously change shape throughout the segment, rising, curling, and receding rather than appearing or being extinguished.
The bright flame column on the right side grows taller and more vertical in the later frames (roughly t=0.7 s onward) compared with the earlier frames.
The yellow folded pieces shift and tilt slightly in place as the fire consumes them; their edges darken and curl over the excerpt.
The reddish ember band in the center glows persistently with minor intensity changes.

The left pillar and top-left logo remain fixed in screen position, indicating the camera is stationary; the right-side bricks become more visible only because of changing firelight, not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of ignition and the identity of the burning material are not shown.
The state of the pile before the segment and its final outcome after the segment are unknown.
Whether the slight piece movements are due to burning collapse, wind, or an unseen hand is not determinable.
uncertain_details: Exact material of the yellow pieces (paper vs. cardboard vs. other) cannot be confirmed.
Minor frame-to-frame jitter could be small camera shake or compression, but no deliberate pan/zoom is evident.
Precise direction of any airflow affecting the flame lean is not certain.
